sections.h2: Where is the Mercer County Recorder and what are its hours?
sections.html:
The Mercer County Recorder is in the courthouse at 101 N. Main Street, Room 203, Celina, Ohio 45822. The phone number is (419) 586-4232. The office opens at 8:30 a.m. every weekday, stays open until 5:00 p.m. on Monday, closes at 4:00 p.m. Tuesday through Friday and shuts on federal holidays.

Documents that touch real estate are recorded here and open to the public. The office takes cash or checks for recording, with no credit cards, and checks should be made out to the Mercer County Recorder. Copies can be paid for by card or eCheck through the office's online payment link.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Mercer County?
sections.html:
The county's fee notice says that since January 1, 2025 a deed, mortgage or lease costs $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. The increase of $5.00 comes from Ohio Senate Bill 94, which took effect October 24, 2024 and allows a document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars. The county prints this page-count schedule:

Mercer County recording fee by page count, as printed on the recorder's page

A $4.00 reference fee and the format rules still apply on top of those figures. Documents with their own statutory fees, such as federal tax liens, plats, zoning papers and UCC filings, do not get the new $5.00 charge.

sections.h2: What format rules can add $20 to a Mercer County deed?
sections.html:
Documents prepared after June 30, 2009 must follow the state's standardization rules in ORC 317.114, or the office collects an extra $20.00. Mercer County lists the guidelines on its recorder pages:

  • Type at least 10 point.
  • Use paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14.
  • Sign and print in black or blue ink only, with no highlighting.
  • Leave one inch of margin on both sides and the bottom of every page.
  • Leave three inches at the top of the first page, which the recorder, auditor and engineer use for their stamps, and one and a half inches on later pages.

Court and taxing authority documents, plats, DD214 forms and state or federal documents are outside the rule. The office also requires an original rather than a photocopy, a legal description, the preparer's name, notarization and English text. A conveyance must stop at the Tax Map office and the auditor before it reaches the recorder.

sections.h2: Can a Mercer County deed be mailed or e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes to both. Since November 1, 2024 the auditor, tax map and recorder offices have accepted deeds and other conveyance papers by mail, and the recorder's notice sets out strict conditions. The legal description must be pre-approved by the Tax Map office, and the packet needs an email showing that approval.

  • Fill out the auditor's forms.
  • Write separate checks to the Mercer County Auditor, the Recorder and the Treasurer. Combined checks cause rejection.
  • Include recording instructions and a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Turnaround is listed as 24 hours by mail and immediate when you deliver in person. The recorder has taken e-recordings since 2010, and since November 5, 2025 conveyance documents may go through each of its three vendors: Simplifile, CSC eRecording and ePN. A title company or lender normally handles that step.

sections.h2: How does the treasurer's office affect a Mercer County sale?
sections.html:
The county treasurer's office is in Room 201 of the courthouse, and its phone number is (419) 586-2259. Its FAQ explains that Ohio collects real estate taxes one year behind, so the closing agreement between buyer and seller decides who covers what. Any tax that comes due after the purchase date becomes the buyer's liability to pay.

Tax bills go out twice a year, usually in January and June, with payment typically due on the 20th in February and July. A payment up to 10 days late draws a 5 percent penalty. After that the penalty is 10 percent. An owner can apply for remission of a penalty, and the county Board of Revision, made up of the treasurer, auditor and a commissioner, considers it. Owners can also arrange monthly payments by ACH or mailed coupons.

A delinquent bill is mailed in late September. The auditor's site says unpaid parcels were advertised on November 4, 2026 unless paid in full or placed on an installment plan by noon on November 2, 2026. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What is changing in Mercer County property values?
sections.html:
The auditor's office is running a 2026 triennial update. It is a data review of arm's-length sale prices from 2023, 2024 and 2025, with no full exterior inspection of every parcel as in the 2023 reappraisal. Updated values will show on the 2027 real estate tax bills.

The auditor also posts a notice about the Inflation Cap Credit created by House Bill 186, now applied to second-half 2025 bills payable in 2026. Each parcel gets its own credit amount, and some parcels get none. Any overpayment carries forward to the first-half 2026 bill. The auditor's site has a conveyance fee calculator, and a seller should use it to get the county's current rate before closing.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Mercer County?
sections.html:
Mercer County is in western Ohio along the Indiana line, with Van Wert, Auglaize, Shelby and Darke counties as its Ohio neighbors. Wikipedia says the county was created in 1820 and organized January 2, 1824. Celina became the seat in 1839, replacing St. Marys. German immigrant farming families settled it in the mid to late 1800s.

Grand Lake St. Marys, the largest inland lake in Ohio according to the auditor's site, sits in the county. The Wabash and St. Marys rivers run through it, and the divide between the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Erie watersheds crosses it. Celina is the only city. Maria Stein is a census-designated place, and fifteen townships fill out the rest. Manufacturing and health care drive jobs, with Celina Insurance Group, Celina Aluminum Precision Technology and J&M Manufacturing among the named employers.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Mercer County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 42,737 residents for July 2025, up 0.5 percent from the 2020 base. Housing figures for 2020 to 2024 show a stable owner market.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 79.6 percent among 16,408 households.
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $210,600.
  • Median monthly owner cost: $1,340 with a mortgage, $553 without.
  • Median gross rent: $804.
  • Median household income: $76,782.
  • Building permits in 2025: 83, against 18,384 housing units.

faqs.q: What are the Mercer County Recorder's hours?
faqs.a: Monday 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office is closed on federal holidays and sits in Room 203 of the courthouse at 101 N. Main Street in Celina.

faqs.q: How much is a one-page or two-page deed in Mercer County?
faqs.a: The county lists $39.00 for either length. Each page after the second adds $8.00, and a $4.00 reference fee or a $20.00 non-standard charge may apply.

faqs.q: Does the Mercer County Recorder take credit cards for recording?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says recording fees are accepted by check or cash only, with checks payable to the Mercer County Recorder. Copy requests can be paid by card or eCheck online.

faqs.q: Is a veteran's discharge free to record in Mercer County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office records a DD214 and issues copies at no charge. Copies are restricted to authorized people with proper identification, such as the veteran or an estate executor.

faqs.q: When did Mercer County start taking conveyance deeds by e-recording?
faqs.a: The recorder's page says conveyance documents have been accepted through each of its three e-recording vendors since November 5, 2025. The county has taken other e-recordings since 2010.
